title: Induction of injective maps on augmented polynomial truncations
statement: Let B and C be commutative rings, C a B-algebra, ε : C → B a B-algebra augmentation, I = ker ε, n a natural number, P = B[X₁,…,Xₙ], and J its variables ideal. Let f : P → C be a B-algebra map with f(J) ⊆ I. Assume C is formally smooth over B and the induced P/J² → C/I² is bijective. Then each induced P/Jᵏ → C/Iᵏ is injective, for every natural k.

proof.text: Use the existing surjectivity theorem to obtain surjectivity at every degree from h₂. In degrees zero and one injectivity is proved directly: the zeroth quotient is trivial, and ε composed with f is constantCoeff since f sends all variables into ker ε. The coefficient characterization of the variables ideal therefore proves its preimage is exactly that ideal. Degree two is the given injectivity.

For r ≥ 2, invert the bijective degree-r map. Compose the inverse with C → C/I^r and lift it across P/J^(r+1) → P/J^r by Mathlib FormallySmooth.liftOfSurjective. The projection kernel is the image of J^r and its square is zero by 2r ≥ r+1. For c ∈ I, choose p representing its lift. Commutativity gives f(p)-c ∈ I^r ⊆ I, so f(p) ∈ I. The proved degree-one injectivity gives p ∈ J. Thus the lift sends I to the image of J, kills I^(r+1), and descends to g : C/I^(r+1) → P/J^(r+1). The composite g f_(r+1) reduces to the identity at degree r. Every assertion in this step is proved in the private helper exists_augmented_truncation_inverse_lift.

Replace explicit polynomial substitution by a general ideal-power estimate. Let L^(r+1)=0 and let e be a ring endomorphism satisfying e(x)-x ∈ L^r for every x, with r ≥ 2. Induction on k, using ideal product induction and e(ab)-ab=(e(a)-a)e(b)+a(e(b)-b), proves e(x)-x ∈ L^(r+k) for x ∈ L^(k+1). If e(z)=0 then z ∈ L^r, and the estimate with k=r-1 gives -z ∈ L^(2r-1) ⊆ L^(r+1)=0. Thus e is injective. Apply this proved estimate to L equal to the image of J in P/J^(r+1) and e=g f_(r+1).

Since g composed with f_(r+1) is injective, f_(r+1) is injective. Pair this with the already known surjectivity to run Nat.le_induction starting at two. Finish with the separate degree-zero and degree-one cases. This is the complete Lean proof and introduces no new sorry.

lean.statement:
theorem bijective_augmented_polynomial_truncations_injective
    (B C : Type u) [CommRing B] [CommRing C] [Algebra B C]
    [FormallySmooth B C] (ε : C →ₐ[B] B) (n : ℕ)
    (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) B →ₐ[B] C)
    (hf : MvPolynomial.idealOfVars (Fin n) B ≤
      (RingHom.ker ε.toRingHom).comap f.toRingHom)
    (h₂ : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMapₐ ((RingHom.ker ε.toRingHom) ^ 2) f
        ((pow_le_pow_left' hf 2).trans (Ideal.le_comap_pow f.toRingHom 2)))) :
    ∀ k : ℕ, Function.Injective
      (Ideal.quotientMapₐ ((RingHom.ker ε.toRingHom) ^ k) f
        ((pow_le_pow_left' hf k).trans (Ideal.le_comap_pow f.toRingHom k)))
